16.title: The Seven Master Spirits
16.b0.ask: “How do the seven Spirits of Paradise leave their mark on our minds, our morals, and even our personalities?”
16.b2.p: In Paper 15 we saw how the seven superuniverses are organized and governed. Paper 16 now turns to the Seven Master Spirits who supervise those superuniverses from Paradise. They are the primary personalities of the Infinite Spirit (16:0.1).
16.b3.p: There are just seven possible associations inherent in three Deities, and in this sevenfold creative act the Infinite Spirit exhausted them all. That is why the universe is run in seven grand divisions and why the number seven is fundamental to its organization (16:0.1). In spirit character the seven are as one, but in every other respect they are very unlike. Each keeps its headquarters on the periphery of Paradise opposite the superuniverse it supervises (16:0.11–12).
16.b4.p: Who, then, are these seven Spirits? And how does their influence reach the basic reactions of our minds, our moral nature, and even our personalities?
16.b5.q: ⟦Q 16:7.10⟧Supreme virtue, then, is wholeheartedly to choose to do the will of the Father in heaven.⟦/Q⟧
16.b8.p: The threefold personalization of Deity holds within it seven possibilities of individual and associative expression. So the plan to create universes that would express the Father, Son, and Spirit made the personalization of the Seven Master Spirits inescapable. If the threefold personalization of Deity is the absolute inevitability, the appearance of the Seven Master Spirits is the subabsolute inevitability (16:1.1).
16.b9.t: The likeness from which it takes origin
16.b10.p: The seven are the eternal portrayal of sevenfold Deity. Through them the Father, the Son, the Spirit, or any pair of them can function as such — but they do not collectively represent the Trinity (16:1.2). Only when all seven assemble about the Conjoint Actor do they represent to the evolving universes the functional power, wisdom, and authority of the Trinity (16:1.3).
16.b12.p: To the universe of universes the Father speaks only through his Son, and the Father and the Son act together only through the Infinite Spirit. Outside of Paradise and Havona, the Infinite Spirit speaks only by the voices of the Seven Master Spirits (16:2.2). So the presence of the Infinite Spirit on any world takes on the color of the unique nature of the Master Spirit who supervises that part of creation (16:2.3).
16.b13.p: The seven together share the supreme-ultimate attributes of the Infinite Spirit, but omnipotence, omniscience, and omnipresence appear only in the group as a whole. As individuals, each is limited to the superuniverse he supervises (16:2.4). Collectively, they are one with the Conjoint Creator on all subabsolute levels (16:2.5).
16.b14.h: 3. Identity and Diversity of the Master Spirits
16.b15.p: The Seven Master Spirits are distinctly personal. They have names, but the paper introduces them by number. They are akin, yet diverse in nature, and this diversity shapes how each governs his superuniverse (16:3.1). In council, each speaks for the Deity from which he takes origin (16:3.2–14).
16.b16.t: Close associate of the chief of Mystery Monitors
All orders of the Sons of God

16.b17.p: Master Spirit Number Seven, who presides over our superuniverse of Orvonton, is a portrait of the three Deities in equal proportions, and he discloses a personal and organic relationship to the Supreme Being. This makes him the presiding head of the council of the Master Spirits (16:3.15). In this age, when the person of the Supreme cannot yet be contacted, Master Spirit Number Seven functions in the place of the God of ascendant creatures in personal relationships (16:3.19).
16.b18.h: 4. Attributes and Functions of the Master Spirits
16.b19.p: The Seven Master Spirits are the full representation of the Infinite Spirit to the evolutionary universes — literally “⟦Q 16:4.1⟧the Seven Spirits of God sent forth to all the universe⟦/Q⟧” (16:4.1). They function on every level of reality except the absolute, and they are the creators of the Universe Power Directors (16:4.2–3). It is also inferred that they joined material and spiritual energies to produce morontia substance and morontia mind, and in this realm they make their great contribution to man’s Paradise ascent (16:4.5–6).
16.b20.t: Where the Master Spirit of Orvonton probably has influence
The life-initiation procedures of the Life Carriers
The life activations of the adjutant mind-spirits
Energy fluctuations in units that respond to linear gravity
The behavior of emergent energy freed from the Unqualified Absolute
The bestowal of the Creative Spirit’s ministry spirit — the Holy Spirit
The bestowal of the spirit of the bestowal Sons — the Spirit of Truth
The reflectivity mechanism of the local universes and the superuniverse
16.b21.p: On the other hand, there are two realms with which they have nothing whatever to do: the bestowal and ministry of the Thought Adjusters, and the functions of the Unqualified Absolute (16:4.16).
16.b23.p: Every world receives the united counsel of all seven Spirits, but the personal touch and tinge of only one (16:5.1). Every creature of the seven superuniverses, man or angel, will forever bear the stamp of its native Master Spirit (16:5.2). The Master Spirits do not directly enter mortal minds; they work through the local universe Creative Spirit, and this Creative Mother Spirit is in nature quite like the Master Spirit of Orvonton (16:5.3).
16.b24.p: Neither Havona training nor Paradise culture erases this stamp. So even in the Corps of the Finality, when the whole evolutionary creation is to be portrayed, a group of seven finaliters is assembled — one from each superuniverse (16:5.5).
16.b26.p: The Master Spirits are the sevenfold source of the cosmic mind. We live under the immediate influence of the Creative Spirit of Nebadon, yet the Master Spirits dominate the basic reactions of all creature mind (16:6.1–2). The cosmic mind has a “reality response” that keeps will creatures from becoming helpless victims of the unspoken assumptions of science, philosophy, and religion (16:6.4).
16.b28.p: When these three cosmic intuitions are unified, they produce a strong character in which a factual science, a moral philosophy, and a genuine religious experience are joined (16:6.10). Sadly, few persons on Urantia take delight in cultivating such courageous and independent cosmic thinking (16:6.9).
16.b29.q: ⟦Q 16:6.11⟧It is the purpose of education to develop and sharpen these innate endowments of the human mind; of civilization to express them; of life experience to realize them; of religion to ennoble them; and of personality to unify them.⟦/Q⟧
16.b31.p: Intelligence alone cannot explain the moral nature. What especially distinguishes man from the animals is his moral and religious nature (16:7.1). An animal learns only by leaping, but a personality can look before it leaps, and so it learns from looking as well. A personality can also judge not only the means but the worth of the goal itself (16:7.3–4).
16.b32.t: By trial and error — by leaping
By insight in advance of experience — by looking as well
The way to reach a goal
Both the way and the worth of the goal itself
16.b33.p: Virtue is righteousness — conformity with the cosmos. To name virtues is not to define them, but to live them is to know them, and virtue is realized by consistently choosing good rather than evil (16:7.6). Morality can never be advanced by law or by force. It must spread by the contagion of contact with morally fragrant persons (16:7.9).
16.b35.p: Personality is a unique gift of the Father, independent of and prior to the bestowal of the Thought Adjuster. Adjusters are identical in nature, but personality is diverse and original (16:8.3). Personality is the part of a person that lets us recognize him as the one we knew, however much his form or mind may have changed (16:8.4). Creature personality is marked by self-consciousness and relative free will (16:8.5).
16.b36.t: Relative free will is involved in
Wholehearted devotion to doing the Father’s will
The sincere pursuit of divine values and wholehearted love of the divine Value-Giver
16.b37.p: The full function of such a personality is the beginning realization of kinship with Deity. A self indwelt by a fragment of God the Father is in truth a spiritual son of God (16:8.19).
16.b39.p: A creature endowed with cosmic mind and indwelt by an Adjuster innately recognizes the reality of energy, mind, and spirit, and so can discern the fact, the law, and the love of God (16:9.1). Personality identity survives in and by the survival of the immortal soul (16:9.3).
16.b40.p: We can be more certain of the presence of God within us than of the reality of our fellows. Social consciousness is a cultural development, so civilizations are unstable; but science, morality, and religion always survive the crash (16:9.4–5). Because we are conscious of God as our Creator Father, we become conscious of man as our brother, and only a God-knowing person can love another as he loves himself (16:9.8, 9.14).
16.b41.t: Recognizing God as a person and our brotherhood with fellow persons
16.b42.q: ⟦Q 16:9.14⟧We worship God, first, because he is, then, because he is in us, and last, because we are in him.⟦/Q⟧
16.b44.p: Paper 16 begins with the seven Spirits of Paradise and comes down to our own minds and personalities. The seven possible unions of the three Deities were personalized as the Seven Master Spirits, and each colors one superuniverse with his own nature. The Seventh Spirit, who cares for our Orvonton, is a balanced portrait of all three Deities and reveals the Supreme Being. And the cosmic mind, whose source they are, lives and works within us as three intuitions: science, morality, and worship. To unify these intuitions is the purpose of personality, and at the end of that road the highest virtue is to choose wholeheartedly to do the Father’s will.

16.b47.box: The intuitions of science, morality, and worship that the Master Spirits have planted in our minds are unified in the choice to do the Father’s will.
17.title: The Seven Supreme Spirit Groups
17.b0.ask: “From the Seven Master Spirits of Paradise down to the adjutant spirits in our own minds, how is the family of spirits joined into one?”
17.b2.p: In Paper 16 we learned who the Seven Master Spirits are and how they leave their mark on our minds. Now Paper 17 introduces a larger family headed by those Master Spirits: the seven Supreme Spirit groups. They are the universal co-ordinating directors of the seven-segmented administration of the grand universe.
17.b3.p: Their field of work begins with the Master Spirits on the periphery of the eternal Isle. It runs through the Havona circuits, the superuniverse governments, and the local universes, and it reaches all the way down to the lowly service of the adjutants bestowed upon the realms of evolutionary mind on the worlds of time and space. In our own Nebadon, the work of the Master Spirit of Orvonton is carried out close at hand by the Creative Mother Spirit on Salvington.
17.b4.p: What, then, does each of these seven groups do, and how do they carry the will of Paradise all the way to our minds?
17.b5.q: ⟦Q 17:8.2⟧The Infinite Spirit, the original and eternal mother of all the angelic ministers.⟦/Q⟧
17.b8.t: Classified as children of the Paradise Trinity
Classified as children of the Paradise Trinity
Classified as children of the Paradise Trinity
Brought into being by the Infinite Spirit and his associates
5. The Seven Spirits of the Circuits
Brought into being by the Infinite Spirit and his associates
Brought into being by the Infinite Spirit and his associates
Brought into being by the Infinite Spirit and his associates
17.b9.p: The Seven Supreme Executives were trinitized by the Father, Son, and Spirit, and they work on the seven Paradise satellites of the Infinite Spirit. In all matters of an executive nature, the Master Spirits act through them. They might be called the board of managing directors of the post-Havona creation, and they see all, hear all, feel all, even know all that happens in the seven superuniverses.
17.b10.p: Yet they do not originate policies or change universe procedures, and they do not interfere with the rule of the Ancients of Days or the sovereignty of the Creator Sons. They are co-ordinators who carry out the combined policies of all duly constituted rulers. Supreme Executive Number Seven, working from the seventh satellite, looks after our own superuniverse — and the name of that satellite is Orvonton. In fact, the superuniverses were named after these satellites.
17.b11.t: Advisory cabinets of a Supreme Executive
Representatives chosen by the children of the Infinite Spirit on each superuniverse headquarters, serving for one millennium
Mortals of Paradise attainment and the trinitized sons of glorified mortals
17.b12.p: So in matters that affect ascending mortals, beings of mortal origin give counsel. And from time to time great reunions take place on these satellites of the Spirit, where ascenders recall the struggles and triumphs of the ascendant career. The Supreme Executives always preside over these fraternal gatherings.
17.b14.p: The Reflective Spirits were created seven at a time, each time by a liaison of the Paradise Trinity with one of the Seven Master Spirits — forty-nine in all. This was the first effort of the Master Spirits to function as cocreators with the Trinity. When the forty-ninth Reflective Spirit had personalized, a new and unexpected reaction occurred in the Deity Absolute, and Majeston, the chief of reflectivity, was personalized.
17.b15.p: Majeston is the only existing personality of divinity created by the Supreme Being in liaison with the Deity Absolute, and his creation was the first supreme creative act of the Supreme Being. The response of the Deity Absolute went far beyond what the Supreme intended. So the author confesses a sense of awe: when the Supreme and the Ultimate reach new levels in ages to come, what other undreamed-of beings might appear?
17.b17.p: Each Reflective Spirit reflects one of the seven possible combinations of the three Deities, so one of each of the seven types is stationed on every superuniverse headquarters. Only in this way can every manifestation of the three Paradise Deities be perfectly reflected. The Deities themselves do not display this power of reflectivity, yet they created the beings who have it.
17.b18.q: ⟦Q 17:3.3⟧Divine heredity does sometimes disclose in the creature certain attributes which are not discernible in the Creator.⟦/Q⟧
17.b19.p: The Reflective Spirits both transmit and preserve. Unlike the official records passed up by the angelic recorders, the true spiritual values are gathered by reflectivity and kept in the living minds of the family of the Infinite Spirit. Reflectivity is also the news-gathering and decree-disseminating mechanism of all creation. It looks automatic, but it is not; it is all very personal and intelligent.
17.b20.t: Dead records, passed up through the angelic recorders
Live records, gathered by reflectivity and preserved in the minds of personalities
17.b22.p: The Reflective Image Aids were created by the Reflective Spirits, and there are just seven of them on each superuniverse headquarters. Each is a true image of its Reflective Mother Spirit — a virtual duplicate, minus the attribute of reflectivity. The Reflective Spirits are of an order that material beings cannot comprehend, and even in their dealings with the Ancients of Days they need the help of their Image Aids.
17.b23.p: The Image Aids seem personal, but they are devoid of will and do not exercise the power of choice. Ascending mortals do not come into close contact with reflectivity itself; some being of reflective nature always stands between us and the actual working of the service.
17.b24.h: 5. The Seven Spirits of the Circuits
17.b25.p: The Seven Spirits of the Circuits are the collective offspring of the Master Spirits, the impersonal representatives who each permeate one of the seven Havona circuits. The Master Spirits give each superuniverse its own distinct character, but through these uniform Circuit Spirits they provide a unified spiritual supervision for the central universe. They contact the beings of Havona through their own offspring, the tertiary supernaphim.
17.b26.t: Never become a permanent part of Havona personalities
17.b27.p: As we pass from circuit to circuit in Havona, we will enjoy their influence and recognize their presence, but we will not be able to hold personal communion with them.
17.b29.p: A local universe Mother Spirit becomes a full person by stages. When a Creator Son is born, the potential of his future consort arises within the Infinite Spirit; she is differentiated through the prayer of a Master Spirit; and she becomes a true person in the era of life creation. The moment when the Universal Father acknowledges the eternal union of the Creator Son and the Creative Spirit is one of the most profoundly touching episodes which ever take place on Paradise.
17.b30.t: Her potential arises with the birth of the Creator Son
She becomes conscious of destiny and gains skill in collaboration
Differentiated by the prayer of a Master Spirit, she goes forth united with the Son
Through the primary eruption she becomes a bona fide person
The Creator Son elevates her to cosovereignty
6. The Ages of Light and Life
A great experience not yet revealed
Thought to be future service together with the Creator Michaels
17.b32.p: The adjutant spirits are the sevenfold mind that a local universe Mother Spirit bestows on the living creatures she creates together with the Creator Son. This bestowal becomes possible when the Creative Spirit is elevated to the prerogatives of personality. Their nature and work are described more fully in the story of Nebadon.
17.b34.p: The seven Supreme Spirit groups form the nucleus of the functional family of the Third Source and Center. Their domain extends from the presence of the Trinity on Paradise to the functioning of mind on the planets of space, and so they unify the descending levels of administration. Together with their Infinite Mother Spirit, they are the immediate creators of all the orders of ministering spirits.
17.b35.t: The Seven Spirits of the Circuits
The angelic orders of the local universes
17.b36.p: The Master Spirits co-ordinate the activities of God the Sevenfold. Collectively they near-equivalate to the divinity level of the Trinity; individually they exhaust the primary associable possibilities of triune Deity; and they hold in trust the sovereignty of the Supreme Being which he does not yet personally exercise. By taking part in the individualization of the Creative Spirits, they contribute to the last level of God the Sevenfold. In the perfected superuniverses of the future, this unity will be inseparable from the experiential sovereignty of the Supreme.
17.b37.q: ⟦Q 17:8.9⟧Functional unity, inherent in the Conjoint Actor, is disclosed to the evolving universes in the Seven Master Spirits, his primary personalities.⟦/Q⟧
17.b39.p: Paper 17 shows us, link by link, the chain of spirit that runs from Paradise to our minds. The Master Spirits set the course, and the Supreme Executives co-ordinate it. The Reflective Spirits and their Image Aids carry the news and values of the whole superuniverse as living records. The Circuit Spirits evenly pervade Havona. And the Creative Spirit stands as the mother of the local universe, reaching our minds through the adjutant mind-spirits. At the root of all these ministering spirits is the Infinite Spirit, the eternal mother of all the angels. Even the small mind each of us has is a gift that comes at the end of this long administration of love, which begins on Paradise.

17.b42.box: From the Seven Master Spirits of Paradise to the adjutant spirits of our minds, the family of spirit is joined in one unbroken ministry.
18.title: The Supreme Trinity Personalities
18.b0.ask: “How do the Trinity personalities, who never fail, govern and help the universe all the way from Paradise to our constellation?”
18.b2.p: In Paper 17 we met the seven Supreme Spirit groups, the functional family of the Infinite Spirit. Now Paper 18 introduces administrators who come directly from the Paradise Trinity: the seven orders of Supreme Trinity Personalities. All of them were designed by the Trinity for specific service.
18.b3.p: Their numbers are definite and final; their creation is a past event, and no more are being personalized. They represent the administrative policies and the justice of the Paradise Trinity, and they form an unbroken line of administration that reaches from the Paradise spheres of the Father to the capitals of the constellations in the local universes. Because they are of divinity essence, there is never any danger of default or risk of rebellion with them.
18.b4.p: Where, then, does each of these seven orders work, and whom will we meet among them as we make our ascent?
18.b5.q: ⟦Q 18:1.5⟧The Paradise Creators respect the privacy and sanctity of personality even in their lowly creatures.⟦/Q⟧
18.b8.t: The seven secret spheres of the Father
18.b9.p: Each of the seven worlds in the innermost circuit of the Paradise satellites is ruled jointly by ten Trinitized Secrets of Supremacy. Seven of them each preside over one of the seven major departments, and the remaining three represent the Father, the Son, and the Spirit. The directors of each sphere resemble the Deity or Deity association that sphere reveals.
18.b10.p: Their work concerns the intimate, personal contact of the Deities with seven basic groups of beings, and so it is truly the Secrets of Supremacy. To all who attain divine perfection the Deities are an open book, yet no one can fully know the personal relations of God with each of his creatures. Even to beings of high attainment these secret worlds ever remain a test of loyalty.
18.b12.p: Each of the billion worlds of Havona is directed by one Eternal of Days. They have ruled from eternity without rotation or reassignment. They are visible to all the will creatures of their domains and preside over the planetary conclaves. When one is absent, his world is directed by a Trinity Teacher Son.
18.b13.p: Each has developed his sphere according to his own ideas and ideals. They visit one another, but they do not copy or imitate; and so every world of Havona is wholly unlike any other. We speak of going “up” to Paradise, but it would be more correct to say we are going inward.
18.b15.p: The Ancients of Days were all trinitized at the same time. The very first entry in the personality records of the universe of universes is the trinitization of these twenty-one beings — hence their name, Ancients of Days. These high beings always govern in groups of three.
18.b16.t: Administrative uniformity and harmony over that diversity
18.b17.p: They are the most powerful of all the direct rulers of the time-space creations, and they alone pass final judgment concerning the eternal extinction of will creatures. Yet they have not experientially earned this right to rule. Sometime they will give way to the Supreme Being, an experiential sovereign, and will become his vicegerents.
18.b18.q: ⟦Q 18:3.9⟧The Supreme Being is achieving the sovereignty of the seven superuniverses by experiential service just as a Creator Son experientially earns the sovereignty of his local universe.⟦/Q⟧
18.b20.p: There are two hundred and ten Perfections of Days, and three of them rule each of the ten major sectors in every superuniverse. They are peculiarly perfect in the mastery of administrative details, hence their name, and they rule as the immediate and personal vicegerents of the Ancients of Days. Most of the administrators who serve under them are seasoned beings who served apprenticeships under the Eternals of Days in Havona.
18.b21.p: After our time in the minor sector, we will go on to Splandon, the headquarters of our major sector, and there we will meet the Perfections of Days. They personally administer the group pledges to the graduates of the major sector schools, and before we reach Uversa we will see all thirty of the Orvonton Perfections of Days.
18.b22.t: The seven educational spheres of a minor sector
The seventy worlds of a major sector
The 490 university worlds of a superuniverse headquarters
18.b24.p: The Recents of Days are the youngest of the supreme directors of the superuniverses. There are twenty-one thousand of them, and in groups of three they preside over the minor sectors. In nature they are co-ordinate with the Perfections of Days, but in administrative authority they are subordinate. Minor sector governments deal very largely with the great physical problems of the superuniverses, and the minor sector spheres are the headquarters of the Master Physical Controllers.
18.b25.p: So the three Recents of Days are seldom together on their capital, but at least one of them always remains on duty. All of us will sometime know the three Recents of Days in charge of Ensa, our minor sector.
18.b27.p: The Trinity personalities of the order of “Days” do not administer below the level of the superuniverse governments; in the local universes they act only as counselors and advisers. Each local universe is assigned one Union of Days, who represents the Trinity and, in some respects, the Universal Father. Because these beings co-ordinate all branches of universal government, they are called Unions of Days.
18.b28.t: The Recents of Days of his minor sector
Data of a physical and semi-intellectual nature
The Perfections of Days of his major sector
The Ancients of Days of his superuniverse
18.b29.p: A Union of Days is not organically connected with the government of his local universe, and he acts only at the request of the local authorities. A Creator Son always has by his side a Paradise brother of Trinity origin, and when the Son is away, the acting rulers are largely guided by this counsel in their major decisions.
18.b31.p: The Faithfuls of Days are the Paradise advisers to the Vorondadek rulers of the hundred constellations in each local universe. They are supremely devoted and divinely faithful to the welfare of their constellations, hence their name. They never take part in administration unless invited by the constellation authorities, and their homes are indeed modest in comparison with those of the Vorondadek rulers.
18.b32.p: The Trinity-origin regime stops with the constellations. The local systems and the inhabited worlds are wholly under the jurisdiction of beings native to the local universes.
18.b34.p: Paper 18 shows us a ladder of Trinity personalities stretching from Paradise to the constellations. In the innermost spheres they guard the personal secrets between God and his creatures. In Havona each one cultivates a world wholly his own. In the superuniverses they lay uniform justice over a diverse creation. And in the local universes and constellations they do not rule but counsel, standing faithfully at the side of those who do. They are perfect beings who never fail; yet because their authority was not earned by experience, they will one day give way to the Supreme Being, the experiential sovereign. We will meet them one after another on our ascent, and in every meeting we will learn that the Creators respect the personality of even the lowliest creature.
18.b35.t: God’s personal relations with his creatures are held sacredly secret
The billion worlds of Havona are each uniquely shaped by their rulers’ own ideals
They set uniform administration over superuniverse diversity and await the Supreme
